## 5. Generic polynomials and dynamics

In this section, we will define a notion of generic polynomials and study its properties, mainly its dynamics. For a pair of polynomials $(f,g)$ with rational coefficients, we first consider three notions of arithmetic complexity, namely $h(f)+h(g)$ , $\langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle$ , and $\log X$ , and show that these are comparable when the pair $(f,g)$ is generic. We then make a detailed study of the equilibrium measures and potentials for generic polynomials at most places. Recall again that for a fixed degree $d$ and $X\geq 1$ , we have the sets

$$ \displaystyle\mathcal{P}(X) \displaystyle=\{z^{d}+a_{d-1}z^{d-1}+\cdots+a_{0}\,|\,a_{i}\in\mathbb{Q},\,H(a_{i})\leq X\}, \displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{c}(X) \displaystyle=\{z^{d}+a_{d-1}z^{d-1}+\cdots+a_{0}\in\mathcal{P}(X)\,|\,a_{d-1}=0\}, $$

### 5.1. Complexity of generic pairs

The arithmetic complexity of a pair $(f,g)\in\mathcal{P}_{c}(X)\times\mathcal{P}(X)$ can be measured by the adelic energy pairing $\langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle$ , by the heights of the polynomials $h(f)+h(g)$ , or simply by the height bound $\log X$ . In this section, we show that these three quantities are comparable in the generic case. We first recall the notion of $\varepsilon$ -ordinary. For an integer $n$ , we let $\operatorname{rad}(n)$ be the product of all distinct prime factors of $n$ .

#### Definition 5.1.

Given $X$ and $\varepsilon>0$ , we will say that a pair $(f,g)\in\mathcal{P}_{c}(X)\times\mathcal{P}(X)$ is $\varepsilon$ -ordinary if

$$ \operatorname{rad}(\operatorname{denom}(c))\geq X^{1-2\varepsilon}\text{ and }\gcd(\operatorname{denom}(c),\operatorname{denom}(c^{\prime}))\leq X^{2\varepsilon}, $$

for any distinct coefficients $c,c^{\prime}$ of $f$ or $g$ .

#### Theorem 5.2.

For any $(f,g)\in\mathcal{P}_{c}(X)\times\mathcal{P}(X)$ , we have

$$ \langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle-2\leq\frac{h(f)+h(g)}{d}\leq 2\log X. $$

Moreover, if $(f,g)$ is $\varepsilon$ -ordinary, then

$$ \langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle+O(d\varepsilon\log X)\geq\frac{h(f)+h(g)}{d}\geq\left(2-O(d\varepsilon+\tfrac{1}{d})\right)\log X. $$

We prove these bounds in Propositions 5.4, 5.11, 5.18 and 5.21. For convenience, we make the following definition.

#### Definition 5.3.

For $v\in M_{K}$ , write $\cal{M}_{f,v}:=\max(1,|a_{d-1}|_{v},\ldots,|a_{0}|_{v})$ .

#### Remark.

Note that $\log\cal{M}_{f,v}$ is the local contribution to the height of $f$ at $v$ , i.e., $h(f)=\frac{1}{[K:\mathbb{Q}]}\sum_{v\in M_{K}}\!n_{v}\log\cal{M}_{f,v}$ . Also, for any place $v^{\prime}$ of a finite extension $K^{\prime}/K$ with $v^{\prime}\mid v$ , we have $\cal{M}_{f,v^{\prime}}=\cal{M}_{f,v}$ .

We begin with an easy bound for $h(f)$ in terms of $\log X$ .

#### Proposition 5.4.

For any $f\in\cal{P}(X)$ , we have $h(f)\leq d\log X$ .

#### Proof.

For any $v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}$ ,

$$ \cal{M}_{f,v}=\max(1,|a_{d-1}|_{v},\ldots,|a_{0}|_{v})\leq\max(1,|a_{d-1}|_{v})\cdots\max(1,|a_{0}|_{v}). $$

Hence

$$ h(f)=\sum_{v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}}\!\log\cal{M}_{f,v}\leq\sum_{v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}}\!\left(\log^{+}|a_{d-1}|_{v}+\cdots+\log^{+}|a_{0}|_{v}\right)=h(a_{d-1})+\cdots+h(a_{0})\leq d\log X.\qed $$

Now we will relate $h(f)+h(g)$ to $\langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle$ . We first note that $\log\cal{M}_{f,v}$ can be read off from the equilibrium potential $G_{f,v}$ at the Gauss point:

#### Lemma 5.5.

Let $v\in M_{K}$ be non-archimedean. Then

$$ G_{f,v}(\zeta(0,1))=\frac{1}{d}\log\cal{M}_{f,v}. $$

#### Proof.

It is routine to check that $f(\zeta(0,1))=\zeta(0,\cal{M}_{f,v})$ , and $f(\zeta(0,R))=\zeta(0,R^{d})$ for all $R\geq\cal{M}_{f,v}$ . Hence for all $n\geq 1$ we have

$$ f^{n}(\zeta(0,1))=\zeta(0,\cal{M}_{f,v}^{d^{n-1}}), $$

and the result follows. ∎

On the other hand, we can bound $G_{f,v}$ in terms of its value at the Gauss point, which in turn yields a bound on the local pairing $-(\mu_{f},\mu_{g})_{v}$ .

#### Lemma 5.6.

Let $v\in M_{K}$ be non-archimedean. For any $\xi\in{\mathbb{A}^{1}_{\operatorname{Berk},v}}$ , we have

$$ G_{f,v}(\xi)\leq\log^{+}|\xi|_{v}+G_{f,v}(\zeta(0,1)). $$

#### Proof.

The left side of the claim is subharmonic on ${\mathbb{A}^{1}_{\operatorname{Berk},v}}$ , while the right side is harmonic on ${\mathbb{A}^{1}_{\operatorname{Berk},v}}\setminus\{\zeta(0,1)\}$ . Hence it suffices to check the inequality for $\xi=\zeta(0,1)$ , where it is clear, and for $|\xi|_{v}\to\infty$ . But $G_{f,v}(\xi)=\log^{+}|\xi|_{v}$ for all $\xi$ with $|\xi|_{v}$ sufficiently large, so we are done by observing that

$$ G_{f,v}(\zeta(0,1))\geq\inf G_{f,v}=I(\mu_{f,v})=0.\qed $$

#### Corollary 5.7.

Let $v\in M_{K}$ be non-archimedean. Then

$$ -(\mu_{f},\mu_{g})_{v}\leq\frac{1}{d}(\log\cal{M}_{f,v}+\log\cal{M}_{g,v}). $$

#### Proof.

We have by Lemmas 5.6 and 5.5,

$$ -(\mu_{f},\mu_{g})_{v}=\int G_{f,v}(\xi)d\mu_{g,v}(\xi)\leq\int\log^{+}|\xi|_{v}d\mu_{g,v}(\xi)+G_{f,v}(\zeta(0,1)) $$

$$ =G_{g,v}(\zeta(0,1))+G_{f,v}(\zeta(0,1))=\frac{1}{d}(\log\cal{M}_{f,v}+\log\cal{M}_{g,v}).\qed $$

The situation at archimedean places $v\mid\infty$ is analogous. As usual, we fix an embedding ${\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{C}$ , and write $|\cdot|_{v}=|\cdot|_{\infty}$ .

#### Lemma 5.8.

We have

$$ \max_{|w|_{\infty}=1}G_{f,\infty}(w)\leq\frac{1}{d}\log\cal{M}_{f,\infty}+1. $$

#### Proof.

Write $|\cdot|=|\cdot|_{\infty}$ and $R=\max(2,\cal{M}_{f,\infty})$ . For $|z|\geq R$ , we have

$$ |f(z)|\leq|z|^{d}+R(|z|^{d-1}+\cdots+|z|+1)\leq(|z|+R)^{d}-R, $$

by comparing terms of the binomial expansion. By induction, we have $|f^{n}(z)|\leq(|z|+R)^{d^{n}}-R$ , so that by the maximum principle we have

$$ G_{f,\infty}(z)\leq\log(\max(|z|,R)+R) $$

for all $z\in\mathbb{C}$ .

Now for $|w|=1$ , we have $|f(w)|\leq dR+1$ . Hence

$$ d\cdot G_{f,\infty}(w)=G_{f,\infty}(f(w))\leq\log(\max(|f(w)|,R)+R)\leq\log((d+1)R+1). $$

If $1\leq\cal{M}_{f,\infty}\leq 2$ then $R=2$ , so

$$ d\cdot G_{f,\infty}(w)\leq\log(2d+3)\leq d\leq\log\cal{M}_{f,\infty}+d. $$

Otherwise, we have $\cal{M}_{f,\infty}>2$ and $R=\cal{M}_{f,\infty}$ , so

$$ d\cdot G_{f,\infty}(w)\leq\log\cal{M}_{f,\infty}+\log(d+2)\leq\log\cal{M}_{f,\infty}+d.\qed $$

#### Lemma 5.9.

For any $z\in\mathbb{C}$ , we have

$$ G_{f,\infty}(z)\leq\log^{+}|z|_{\infty}+\max_{|w|_{\infty}=1}G_{f,\infty}(w). $$

#### Proof.

Write $|\cdot|=|\cdot|_{\infty}$ . The left side of the claim is subharmonic on $\mathbb{C}$ , while the right side is harmonic on $\mathbb{C}\setminus\partial B(0,1)$ . Hence it suffices to check the inequality on $|z|=1$ , where it is clear, and for $|z|\to\infty$ . But $G_{f,\infty}(z)-\log^{+}|z|\to 0$ as $|z|\to\infty$ , so we are done by observing that

$$ \max_{|w|=1}G_{f,\infty}(w)\geq\inf G_{f,\infty}=I(\mu_{f,\infty})=0.\qed $$

#### Corollary 5.10.

We have

$$ -(\mu_{f},\mu_{g})_{\infty}\leq\frac{1}{d}(\log\cal{M}_{f,\infty}+\log\cal{M}_{g,\infty})+2. $$

#### Proof.

We have by Lemmas 5.9 and 5.8

$$ -(\mu_{f},\mu_{g})_{\infty}=\int G_{f,\infty}(z)d\mu_{g,\infty}(z)\leq\max_{|w|_{\infty}=1}G_{f,\infty}(w)+\int\log^{+}|z|_{\infty}d\mu_{g,\infty}(z)=\max_{|w|_{\infty}=1}G_{f,\infty}(w)-(\mu_{S^{1}},\mu_{g,\infty})_{\infty} $$

$$ =\max_{|w|_{\infty}=1}G_{f,\infty}(w)+\int G_{g,\infty}(e^{i\theta})\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}\leq\max_{|w|_{\infty}=1}G_{f,\infty}(w)+\max_{|w|_{\infty}=1}G_{g,\infty}(w)\leq\frac{1}{d}(\log\cal{M}_{f,\infty}+\log\cal{M}_{g,\infty})+2.\qed $$

Combining the above results, we obtain the following bound on the adelic energy pairing $\langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle$ .

#### Proposition 5.11.

We have

$$ \langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle\leq\frac{h(f)+h(g)}{d}+2. $$

#### Proof.

Since $(\mu_{f},\mu_{f})_{v}=(\mu_{g},\mu_{g})_{v}=0$ , we have

$$ \langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}}\!(\mu_{f}-\mu_{g},\mu_{f}-\mu_{g})_{v}=\sum_{v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}}\!-(\mu_{f},\mu_{g})_{v}. $$

Now each term in the sum is bounded by Corollaries 5.7 and 5.10; summing over all places, we obtain the desired bound. ∎

Our next objective is to show that most pairs $(f,g)\in\mathcal{P}_{c}(X)\times\mathcal{P}(X)$ are $\varepsilon$ -ordinary, which requires some preparatory estimates.

#### Proposition 5.12 ([LM21, Lem. 2.9]).

Fix $\varepsilon>0$ . Then for all large enough $X$ ,

$$ \sum_{n\leq X}\frac{1}{\operatorname{rad}(n)}\leq X^{\varepsilon}. $$

#### Corollary 5.13.

There are at most $O_{\varepsilon}(X^{2-\varepsilon})$ rationals $x$ such that $h(x)\leq\log X$ and $\operatorname{rad}(\operatorname{denom}(x))\leq X^{1-2\varepsilon}$ .

#### Proof.

By Proposition 5.12, the number of possible values of $\operatorname{denom}(x)$ is

$$ \#\{n\leq X\,:\,\operatorname{rad}(n)\leq X^{1-2\varepsilon}\}\lesssim_{\varepsilon}X^{\varepsilon}X^{1-2\varepsilon}=X^{1-\varepsilon}, $$

and for each such denominator there are at most $2X+1$ possibilities for $x$ . ∎

#### Lemma 5.14.

Let $x_{1},x_{2}$ be chosen uniformly at random independently from the finite set $\{x\in\mathbb{Q}\,:\,h(x)\leq\log X\}$ , and write $x_{i}=\frac{\alpha_{i}}{\beta_{i}}$ for some $|\alpha_{i}|\leq X$ , $1\leq\beta_{i}\leq X$ , $\gcd(\alpha_{i},\beta_{i})=1$ . Then

$$ \Pr(\gcd(\beta_{1},\beta_{2})\geq X^{2\varepsilon})\lesssim_{\varepsilon}X^{-\varepsilon}. $$

#### Proof.

Fix $x_{1}$ . If $\gcd(\beta_{1},\beta_{2})\geq X^{2\varepsilon}$ , then $\beta_{2}=km$ for some $k,m$ satisfying

$$ m\mid\beta_{1},\quad m\geq X^{2\varepsilon},\quad km\leq X. $$

Since $\beta_{1}\leq X$ , the number of divisors of $\beta_{1}$ is at most $O_{\varepsilon}(X^{\varepsilon})$ , by the divisor bound. Hence there are at most $O_{\varepsilon}(X^{\varepsilon})$ choices for $m$ , and for each such $m$ there are at most $X^{1-2\varepsilon}$ choices for $k$ . Also, for each $\beta_{2}$ there are at most $X$ choices for $\alpha_{2}$ . Thus there are $\lesssim_{\varepsilon}X^{\varepsilon}\cdot X^{1-2\varepsilon}\cdot X=X^{2-\varepsilon}$ choices for $x_{2}$ , out of $\sim X^{2}$ possibilities from $\{x\in\mathbb{Q}\,:\,h(x)\leq\log X\}$ by eq. 8. Hence

$$ \Pr(\gcd(\beta_{1},\beta_{2})\geq X^{2\varepsilon}\,|\,\beta_{1}\text{ is fixed})\lesssim_{\varepsilon}\frac{X^{2-\varepsilon}}{X^{2}}=X^{-\varepsilon}, $$

which implies the desired statement. ∎

#### Proposition 5.15.

The proportion of pairs $(f,g)\in\mathcal{P}_{c}(X)\times\mathcal{P}(X)$ which are $\varepsilon$ -ordinary is $1-O_{\varepsilon}(d^{2}X^{-\varepsilon})$ .

#### Proof.

By Corollary 5.13, there is at most an $O_{\varepsilon}(dX^{-\varepsilon})$ proportion of polynomials $f\in\mathcal{P}_{c}(X)$ where $\operatorname{rad}(\operatorname{denom}(a_{i}))\leq X^{1-2\varepsilon}$ for some $i$ ; the analogous bound holds for $g$ . Also, by Lemma 5.14, there is at most an $O_{\varepsilon}(d^{2}X^{-\varepsilon})$ proportion of pairs $(f,g)\in\mathcal{P}_{c}(X)\times\mathcal{P}(X)$ where $\gcd(\operatorname{denom}(a_{i}),\operatorname{denom}(b_{j}))>X^{2\varepsilon}$ for some $i,j$ .

Hence at most $O_{\varepsilon}(d^{2}X^{-\varepsilon})$ proportion of pairs $(f,g)$ satisfies one of the above conditions; this is equivalent to not being $\varepsilon$ -ordinary, and we are done. ∎

We now show that for $\varepsilon$ -ordinary pairs, the reverse inequalities to Propositions 5.4 and 5.11 hold up to a small multiplicative error.

#### Definition 5.16.

Given a pair $(f,g)$ , and $0\leq j\leq d-1$ , we say that a non-archimedean place $v\in M_{K}$ is associated to $a_{j}$ if

$$ \forall i\neq j\,[|a_{i}|_{v}\leq 1],\quad\forall i\,[|b_{i}|_{v}\leq 1],\quad|a_{j}|_{v}>1. $$

We define places associated to $b_{j}$ similarly.

We call a non-archimedean place $v\in M_{K}$ a good place for the pair $(f,g)$ if $v$ is associated to some coefficient $a_{j}$ or $b_{j}$ , or a bad place for $(f,g)$ otherwise. (We will always treat archimedean places separately.)

#### Remark.

Each $v\in M_{K}$ is associated to at most one coefficient of $f$ or $g$ . If $v$ is associated to $a_{j}$ , then $\cal{M}_{f,v}=|a_{j}|_{v}>1$ and $\cal{M}_{g,v}=1$ , and similarly for $b_{j}$ .

We first show the reverse bound to Proposition 5.4 for $h(f)+h(g)$ and $\log X$ .

#### Lemma 5.17.

For any $\varepsilon$ -ordinary pair $(f,g)\in\mathcal{P}_{c}(X)\times\mathcal{P}(X)$ , we have

$$ \frac{1}{[K:\mathbb{Q}]}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}v\in M_{K}\\
v\text{ assoc.\ }a_{j}\end{subarray}}\!\!n_{v}\log|a_{j}|_{v}\geq(1-O(d\varepsilon))\log X, $$

and similarly for $b_{j}$ .

#### Proof.

We may assume that $K=\mathbb{Q}$ . Let $A_{i},B_{i}$ denote the denominators of $a_{i},b_{i}$ respectively. Now $v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}$ is associated to $a_{j}$ if and only if $v$ divides $A_{j}$ , but no other $A_{i}$ or $B_{i}$ ; hence

$$ \sum_{v\text{ assoc.\ }a_{j}}\!\!\log|a_{j}|_{v}\geq\log\operatorname{rad}(A_{j})-\sum_{i\neq j}\log\gcd(A_{i},A_{j})-\sum_{i}\log\gcd(B_{i},A_{j}) $$

$$ \geq(1-2\varepsilon)\log X-(2d-1)2\varepsilon\log X\geq(1-4d\varepsilon)\log X. $$

The argument for $b_{j}$ is analogous. ∎

#### Proposition 5.18.

For any $\varepsilon$ -ordinary pair $(f,g)\in\mathcal{P}_{c}(X)\times\mathcal{P}(X)$ , we have

$$ \frac{h(f)+h(g)}{d}\geq\left(2-O(d\varepsilon+\tfrac{1}{d})\right)\log X. $$

#### Proof.

Using Lemma 5.17, we have

$$ h(f)+h(g)=\sum_{v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}}\!(\log\mathcal{M}_{f,v}+\log\mathcal{M}_{g,v})\geq\sum_{j}\sum_{v\text{ assoc.\ }a_{j}}\!\!\log|a_{j}|_{v}+\sum_{j}\sum_{v\text{ assoc.\ }b_{j}}\!\!\log|b_{j}|_{v} $$

$$ \geq(2d-1)(1-4d\varepsilon)\log X\geq 2d\left(1-O(d\varepsilon+\tfrac{1}{d})\right)\log X, $$

and we are done after dividing by $d$ . ∎

we now proceed to show the reverse bound to Proposition 5.11 for $h(f)+h(g)$ and $\langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle$ . We begin by observing an important equality case for Corollary 5.7.

#### Proposition 5.19.

Let $v\in M_{K}$ be non-archimedean. If $v$ is good for $(f,g)$ , then

$$ -(\mu_{f},\mu_{g})_{v}=\frac{1}{d}(\log\mathcal{M}_{f,v}+\log\mathcal{M}_{g,v}). $$

#### Proof.

Assume that $g$ has explicit good reduction at $v$ ; in particular, $\mathcal{M}_{g,v}=1$ and $\mu_{g,v}=\delta_{\zeta(0,1)}$ . Now by Lemma 5.5,

$$ -(\mu_{f},\mu_{g})_{v}=\int G_{f,v}\operatorname{d}\mu_{g,v}=G_{f,v}(\zeta(0,1))=\frac{1}{d}\log\mathcal{M}_{f,v}=\frac{1}{d}(\log\mathcal{M}_{f,v}+\log\mathcal{M}_{g,v}). $$

The argument when $f$ has explicit good reduction is analogous. ∎

Next, for an $\varepsilon$ -ordinary pair $(f,g)$ , we show that the local contribution to $h(f)+h(g)$ from bad places is small.

#### Proposition 5.20.

For any $\varepsilon$ -ordinary pair $(f,g)\in\mathcal{P}_{c}(X)\times\mathcal{P}(X)$ , we have

$$ \frac{1}{[K:\mathbb{Q}]}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}v\in M_{K}\\
v\text{ bad}\end{subarray}}\!n_{v}(\log\cal{M}_{f,v}+\log\cal{M}_{g,v})\lesssim d^{2}\varepsilon\log X. $$

#### Proof.

We may assume that $K=\mathbb{Q}$ . Write $A_{i},B_{i}$ for the denominator of $a_{i},b_{i}$ respectively. Let $p_{v}$ denote the prime associated to a place $v$ . Now

$$ \sum_{v\text{ bad}}\log\cal{M}_{f,v}\leq\sum_{v\text{ bad}}\log p_{v}+\sum_{v\text{ bad}}\max_{i}(0,\log|a_{i}|_{v}-\log p_{v}). $$

Note that $v$ is a bad place if and only if $p_{v}$ divides more than one of the $A_{i}$ or $B_{i}$ . Hence the first sum on the right in (9) is

$$ \sum_{v\text{ bad}}\log p_{v}\leq\sum_{i,j}\log\gcd(A_{i},B_{j})+\sum_{i<j}\log\gcd(A_{i},A_{j})+\sum_{i<j}\log\gcd(B_{i},B_{j})\leq 4d^{2}\varepsilon\log X. $$

Also, the second term on the right in (9) is

$$ \sum_{v\text{ bad}}\max_{i}(0,\log|a_{i}|_{v}-\log p_{v})\leq\sum_{i}\sum_{v\nmid\infty}\max(0,\log|a_{i}|_{v}-\log p_{v})=\sum_{i}(\log A_{i}-\log\operatorname{rad}(A_{i})) $$

$$ \leq\sum_{i}(\log X-\log X^{1-2\varepsilon})\leq 2d\varepsilon\log X. $$

Substituting back into (9), we get $\sum_{v\text{ bad}}\log\cal{M}_{f,v}\lesssim d^{2}\varepsilon\log X$ . The same argument works for $g$ . ∎

#### Proposition 5.21.

For any $\varepsilon$ -ordinary pair $(f,g)\in\mathcal{P}_{c}(X)\times\mathcal{P}(X)$ , we have

$$ \langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle\geq\frac{h(f)+h(g)}{d}-O((d\varepsilon+\tfrac{1}{d})\log X). $$

#### Proof.

We may assume that $K=\mathbb{Q}$ . Note that $(\mu_{f},\mu_{f})_{v}=(\mu_{g},\mu_{g})_{v}=0$ for any $v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}$ , so $0\leq(\mu_{f}-\mu_{g},\mu_{f}-\mu_{g})_{v}=-2(\mu_{f},\mu_{g})_{v}$ . Hence by Proposition 5.19

$$ \langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle\geq\sum_{v\text{ good}}-(\mu_{f},\mu_{g})_{v}=\frac{1}{d}\sum_{v\text{ good}}(\log\mathcal{M}_{f,v}+\log\mathcal{M}_{g,v})=\frac{h(f)+h(g)}{d}-\frac{1}{d}\sum_{v\text{ bad}}(\log\mathcal{M}_{f,v}+\log\mathcal{M}_{g,v}). $$

Using Proposition 5.20, we get the above expression is

$$ =\frac{h(f)+h(g)}{d}-\frac{1}{d}(\log\mathcal{M}_{f,\infty}+\log\mathcal{M}_{g,\infty})\geq\frac{h(f)+h(g)}{d}-O(d\varepsilon\log X)-O(\tfrac{1}{d}\log X).\qed $$

### 5.2. Dynamics on generic polynomials

For $\varepsilon$ -ordinary pairs $(f,g)$ , since the denominators of the coefficients are almost pairwise coprime, most primes which divide one such denominator would not divide any other denominator. Hence for most places $v$ where $f,g$ do not both have explicit good reduction, it will be the case that one of them has explicit good reduction, while the other has exactly one large coefficient.

We know in the former that the equilibrium measure and potential are $\delta_{\zeta(0,1)}$ and $\log^{+}|\cdot|_{v}$ respectively; in this section, we will study the equilibrium measure and potential for the latter case.

First, we show that the equilibrium measure lies in three distinct strata (cf. Proposition 4.3, which corresponds to the case $j=0$ ).

#### Proposition 5.22.

Let $v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}$ be non-archimedean with $|a_{0}|_{v}=1$ . If there exists $1\leq j\leq d-1$ such that

$$ \forall i\neq j\,[|a_{i}|_{v}\leq 1],\quad|a_{j}|_{v}>1, $$

then $|\zeta|_{v}\in\{|a_{j}|_{v}^{\frac{1}{d-j}},|a_{j}|_{v}^{\frac{1}{j}(\frac{1}{d-j}-1)},|a_{j}|_{v}^{-\frac{1}{j}}\}$ for all $\zeta\in K_{f,v}$ .

#### Proof.

By the density of Type I points in $K_{f,v}$ , it suffices to prove the statement for $\zeta=z\in\mathbb{C}_{v}$ . We will prove the contrapositive statement, so suppose that $|z|_{v}$ is not one of the listed values.

Case 1a: $|z|_{v}\geq 1$ and $j<d-1$ . Then $|z^{d}|_{v}\not=|a_{j}z^{j}|_{v}$ by assumption, so

$$ |f(z)|_{v}=\max(|z^{d}|_{v},|a_{j}z^{j}|_{v})>|a_{j}|_{v}^{\frac{1}{d-j}}. $$

By induction, we have $|f^{n}(z)|_{v}=|f(z)|_{v}^{d^{n-1}}$ ; in particular, $f^{n}(z)\to\infty$ , so $z\not\in K_{f,v}$ .

Case 1b: $|z|_{v}\geq 1$ and $j=d-1$ . Note that $|z|_{v}\not=|a_{j}|_{v}^{\frac{1}{j}(\frac{1}{d-j}-1)}=1$ , so $|z|_{v}>1$ , and now the argument of Case 1a works verbatim.

Case 2: $|z|_{v}<1$ . Then $|a_{j}z^{j}|_{v}\not=1$ and $|a_{0}|_{v}=1$ by assumption, so

$$ |f(z)|_{v}=\max(|a_{j}z^{j}|_{v},1)\geq 1. $$

Furthermore, $|a_{j}z^{j}|_{v}\not=|a_{j}|_{v}^{\frac{1}{d-j}}$ by assumption, so $f(z)\not\in K_{f,v}$ by Cases 1a and 1b. Thus $z\not\in K_{f,v}$ as well. ∎

The next result shows that if some subset of ${\mathbb{A}^{1}_{\operatorname{Berk},v}}$ decomposes into finitely many strata, then the equilibrium measure restricted to each stratum is a multiple of the equilibrium measure on that stratum.

#### Lemma 5.23.

Let $r_{1}>r_{2}>\cdots>r_{k}>0$ , and let $K_{i}\subseteq\overline{D}_{\operatorname{an}}(0,r_{i})\setminus D_{\operatorname{an}}(0,r_{i})$ be compact sets in ${\mathbb{A}^{1}_{\operatorname{Berk},v}}$ with equilibrium measures $\mu_{i}$ . Then the equilibrium measure $\mu$ on $K=\bigcup_{i=1}^{k}K_{i}$ is a convex combination of the $\mu_{i}$ .

#### Proof.

Write $\mu=\sum_{i=1}^{k}\alpha_{i}\nu_{i}$ for some $\alpha_{i}\in[0,1]$ and $\nu_{i}$ probability measures supported on $\overline{D}_{\operatorname{an}}(0,r_{i})\setminus D_{\operatorname{an}}(0,r_{i})$ . Now for all $i<j$ and all $\zeta_{i}\in K_{i}$ , $\zeta_{j}\in K_{j}$ , we have $\delta(\zeta_{i},\zeta_{j})_{\infty}=\log r_{i}$ , so

$$ I(\mu)=\sum_{i=1}^{k}\alpha_{i}^{2}I(\nu_{i})+\sum_{\mathclap{1\leq i<j\leq k}}2\alpha_{i}\alpha_{j}\log r_{i}. $$

Since $\mu$ is the equilibrium measure on $K$ , the above expression is minimal over all choices of $\nu_{i}$ supported on $K_{i}$ . But the minimizer of $I(\nu_{i})$ for $\nu_{i}$ supported on $K_{i}$ is precisely $\mu_{i}$ ; hence $\nu_{i}=\mu_{i}$ when $\alpha_{i}\neq 0$ , and so $\mu=\sum_{i=1}^{k}\alpha_{i}\mu_{i}$ .

∎

#### Remark.

The above result is known in more general contexts, cf. [Rum89, Rum13].

#### Theorem 5.24.

Let $f,v,j$ be as in Proposition 5.22, and write

$$ r_{1}=|a_{j}|_{v}^{\frac{1}{d-j}},\qquad r_{2}=|a_{j}|_{v}^{\frac{1}{j}(\frac{1}{d-j}-1)},\qquad r_{3}=|a_{j}|_{v}^{-\frac{1}{j}}. $$

Let $\mu_{f,v}=\alpha_{1}\mu_{1}+\alpha_{2}\mu_{2}+\alpha_{3}\mu_{3}$ for some $\alpha_{i}\in[0,1]$ and $\mu_{i}$ probability measures supported on the strata $S_{i}:=\overline{D}_{\operatorname{an}}(0,r_{i})\setminus D_{\operatorname{an}}(0,r_{i})$ . Then

$$ \displaystyle\alpha_{1} \displaystyle=\frac{d-j}{d}, \displaystyle I(\mu_{1}) \displaystyle=-\frac{j}{(d-j)^{2}}\log|a_{j}|_{v}, \displaystyle\alpha_{2} \displaystyle=\frac{j(d-j)}{d^{2}}, \displaystyle I(\mu_{2}) \displaystyle=-\left(\frac{1}{j}+\frac{1}{(d-j)^{2}}\right)\log|a_{j}|_{v}, \displaystyle\alpha_{3} \displaystyle=\frac{j^{2}}{d^{2}}, \displaystyle I(\mu_{3}) \displaystyle=-\left(\frac{1}{j}+\frac{1}{j^{2}}\right)\log|a_{j}|_{v}. $$

0&j&j\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}\alpha_{1}\\
\alpha_{2}\\
\alpha_{3}\end{pmatrix}. $$

Combined with $\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2}+\alpha_{3}=1$ , we find that indeed

$$ \begin{pmatrix}\alpha_{1}\\
\alpha_{2}\\
\alpha_{3}\end{pmatrix}=\frac{1}{d^{2}}\begin{pmatrix}d(d-j)\\
j(d-j)\\
j^{2}\end{pmatrix}. $$

We now compute the energies $I(\mu_{i})$ . By eq. 10,

$$ 0=I(\mu_{f,v})=I(\alpha_{1}\mu_{1}+\alpha_{2}\mu_{2}+\alpha_{3}\mu_{3})=\alpha_{1}^{2}I(\mu_{1})+\alpha_{2}^{2}I(\mu_{2})+\alpha_{3}^{2}I(\mu_{3}) $$

$$ +2\alpha_{1}\alpha_{2}\log(r_{1})+2\alpha_{1}\alpha_{3}\log(r_{1})+2\alpha_{2}\alpha_{3}\log(r_{2}). $$

But taking the sum of $\alpha_{i}$ times the $i$ -th expression above, we recover the expression for $I(\mu_{f,v})$ , which has value $0$ ; hence each of the above expressions is $0$ . Now we get the claimed values of $I(\mu_{i})$ by isolating them within each expression.

∎

#### Corollary 5.25.

In the setting of Theorem 5.24, we have

$$ G_{f,v}(\xi)\leq\begin{cases}\log|\xi|_{v}&\text{if }|\xi|_{v}\in[r_{1},\infty)\\
\frac{j}{d}\log|\xi|_{v}+\frac{1}{d}\log|a_{j}|_{v}&\text{if }|\xi|_{v}\in[r_{2},r_{1}]\\
\frac{j^{2}}{d^{2}}\log|\xi|_{v}+\frac{j+1}{d^{2}}\log|a_{j}|_{v}&\text{if }|\xi|_{v}\in[r_{3},r_{2}]\\
\frac{1}{d^{2}}\log|a_{j}|_{v}&\text{if }|\xi|_{v}\in[0,r_{3}],\end{cases} $$

with equality when $|\xi|_{v}\not\in\{r_{1},r_{2},r_{3}\}$ .

#### Proof.

We have $G_{f,v}=\alpha_{1}G_{\mu_{1}}+\alpha_{2}G_{\mu_{2}}+\alpha_{3}G_{\mu_{3}}$ , where $G_{\mu_{i}}$ is the equilibrium potential for $\mu_{i}$ . Since $|w|_{v}=r_{i}$ for all $w\in\operatorname{supp}\mu_{i}$ , we have

$$ G_{\mu_{i}}(\xi)=\int\delta(\xi,w)_{\infty}d\mu_{i}(w)\leq\log\max(|\xi|_{v},r_{i}), $$

with equality when $|\xi|_{v}\neq r_{i}$ . The claim follows by routine computation. ∎

We conclude this section by computing the capacities and potentials on some sets we will use in Section 6.

#### Lemma 5.26.

Let $s_{1}>s_{2}>0$ , and let $K_{i}\subseteq\overline{D}_{\operatorname{an}}(0,s_{i})\setminus D_{\operatorname{an}}(0,s_{i})$ be compact sets with equilibrium measures $\nu_{i}$ . Then the equilibrium measure $\nu$ on $K=K_{1}\cup K_{2}$ is given by $\nu=\alpha_{1}\nu_{1}+\alpha_{2}\nu_{2}$ for some $\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2}\in[0,1]$ .

Moreover, we have

$$ I(\nu)=\frac{\log^{2}s_{1}-I(\nu_{1})I(\nu_{2})}{2\log s_{1}-I(\nu_{1})-I(\nu_{2})}. $$

#### Proof.

By Lemma 5.23, $\nu$ has the given form. Now

$$ I(\nu)=a\alpha_{1}^{2}+b\alpha_{2}^{2}+2c\alpha_{1}\alpha_{2},\  $$

where $a=I(\nu_{1})$ , $b=I(\nu_{2})$ , and $c=\log s_{1}$ . It is easy to verify (e.g., by Lagrange multipliers) that this quadratic form is minimized on $\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2}=1$ at

$$ (\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2})=\left(\frac{c-b}{2c-a-b},\frac{c-a}{2c-a-b}\right). $$

Since $K_{1},K_{2}\subseteq\overline{D}_{\operatorname{an}}(0,s_{1})$ , we have $a,b\leq V(\overline{D}_{\operatorname{an}}(0,s_{1}))=c$ , so $\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2}\in[0,1]$ . Finally, substituting the values of $\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2}$ into eq. 11 yields $I(\nu)=\frac{c^{2}-ab}{2c-a-b}$ . ∎

#### Proposition 5.27.

In the setting of Theorem 5.24, define $\mathcal{R}=|a_{j}|_{v}^{j/(d^{2}-j^{2})}$ ,

$$ S_{f,v}^{\cup}=\{\zeta(0,\mathcal{R})\}\cup\operatorname{supp}\mu_{1},\qquad S_{f,v}^{\cap}=\operatorname{supp}\mu_{2}\cup\operatorname{supp}\mu_{3}. $$

Then

#### Proof.

Write $\nu_{f,v}^{\cup},\nu_{f,v}^{\cap}$ for the equilibrium measures on $S_{f,v}^{\cup},S_{f,v}^{\cap}$ respectively. Then

$$ \nu_{f,v}^{\cup}=\alpha\mu_{1}+\beta\delta_{\zeta(0,\mathcal{R})},\qquad\nu_{f,v}^{\cap}=\alpha^{\prime}\mu_{2}+\beta^{\prime}\mu_{3}. $$

By Corollary 5.25, the values of $G_{f,v}$ and $\log^{+}|\cdot|_{v}$ on each of the pieces are given as follows. These yield the identities in the left column of the claim.

$$ \begin{array}[]{rcc}&G_{f,v}&\log^{+}|\cdot|_{v}\\
\hline\cr\zeta(0,\mathcal{R})&\frac{d}{d^{2}-j^{2}}\log|a_{j}|_{v}&\frac{j}{d^{2}-j^{2}}\log|a_{j}|_{v}\\
\operatorname{supp}\mu_{1}&0&\frac{1}{d-j}\log|a_{j}|_{v}\\
\overline{D}_{\operatorname{an}}(0,1)&\leq\frac{1}{d}\log|a_{j}|_{v}&0\\
\operatorname{supp}\mu_{2}&0&0\\
\operatorname{supp}\mu_{3}&0&0\end{array} $$

$$ I(\nu_{f,v}^{\cup})=\frac{\log^{2}r_{1}-I(\mu_{1})\log\mathcal{R}}{2\log r_{1}-I(\mu_{1})-\log\mathcal{R}},\quad I(\nu_{f,v}^{\cap})=\frac{\log^{2}r_{2}-I(\mu_{2})I(\mu_{3})}{2\log r_{2}-I(\mu_{2})-I(\mu_{3})}. $$

## 6. Shared Small Points on average

Let $f,g$ be polynomials of degree $d\geq 2$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ . We will now prove Theorem 1.6 on the essential minimum of $\widehat{h}_{f}+\widehat{h}_{g}$ for generic pairs $(f,g)$ . We first start off with some results that apply to all pairs $(f,g)$ , before specializing to the generic case.

Let $\overline{L}_{f}$ be the canonical adelic line bundle associated to our polynomial $f\in\mathbb{Q}[z]$ of degree $d\geq 2$ . For background on adelic line bundles, readers may refer to [PST12]. Then the height associated to $\overline{L}_{f}$ is the canonical height $h_{f}$ , and so applying Zhang’s inequality [Zha95, Thm. 1.10] to the line bundle $\overline{L}_{f\otimes g}=\overline{L}_{f}\otimes\overline{L}_{g}$ gives us

$$ \liminf_{\mathbb{P}^{1}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})}\left(\widehat{h}_{f}+\widehat{h}_{g}\right)+\inf_{\mathbb{P}^{1}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})}\left(\widehat{h}_{f}+\widehat{h}_{g}\right)\leq\langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle\leq 2\liminf_{\mathbb{P}^{1}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})}\left(\widehat{h}_{f}+\widehat{h}_{g}\right). $$

Since $f$ and $g$ are both polynomials, $\infty$ is a common preperiodic point and thus we have $\inf(\widehat{f}+\widehat{g})=0$ . We then get

$$ \frac{1}{2}\langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle\leq\liminf_{\mathbb{P}^{1}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})}\left(\widehat{h}_{f}+\widehat{h}_{g}\right)\leq\langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle. $$

When $\langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle=0$ , this implies that $\liminf(\widehat{h}_{f}+\widehat{h}_{g})=0$ , but in general only gives a possible range. We now give a different proof of (12) using equidistribubtion and the energy pairing. We first prove the upper bound, which is an easy consequence of the Arakelov–Zhang pairing in [PST12].

#### Proposition 6.1.

$\displaystyle\liminf_{x\in{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}}\left(\widehat{h}_{f}(x)+\widehat{h}_{g}(x)\right)\leq\langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle$ .

#### Proof.

Let $(x_{n})$ be a sequence of pairwise distinct points in ${\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}$ with $\widehat{h}_{f}(x_{n})\to 0$ (for instance from $\operatorname{Prep}(f)$ , which is infinite). By [PST12, Thm. 1], we have $\widehat{h}_{g}(x_{n})\to\langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle$ , so $\langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle$ is a limit point for the values of $\widehat{h}_{f}+\widehat{h}_{g}$ on ${\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}$ . ∎

We next do the lower bound.

#### Proposition 6.2.

$\displaystyle\liminf_{x\in\mathbb{\overline{Q}}}\left(\widehat{h}_{f}(x)+\widehat{h}_{g}(x)\right)\geq\frac{1}{2}\langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle$ .

#### Proof.

Given $x\in\mathbb{\overline{Q}}$ , write $F\subseteq\mathbb{\overline{Q}}$ for its $\operatorname{Gal}({\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}/\mathbb{Q})$ -orbit, and let $N=|F|$ . Let $K$ be a number field containing $F$ , and let $\varepsilon=\{\varepsilon_{v}\}_{v\in M_{K}}$ be the adelic radius given in the proof of Theorem 3.18.

Recall the parallelogram law for bilinear forms $(\cdot,\cdot)$ :

$$ (a+b,a+b)+(a-b,a-b)=2(a,a)+2(b,b). $$

Applying this for $a=\frac{\mu_{f}+\mu_{g}}{2}-[F]_{\varepsilon}$ , $b=\frac{\mu_{f}-\mu_{g}}{2}$ , $(\cdot,\cdot)=(\cdot,\cdot)_{v}$ , we have

$$ (\mu_{f}-[F]_{\varepsilon},\mu_{f}-[F]_{\varepsilon})_{v}+(\mu_{g}-[F]_{\varepsilon},\mu_{g}-[F]_{\varepsilon})_{v} $$

$$ =2\left(\frac{\mu_{f}+\mu_{g}}{2}-[F]_{\varepsilon},\frac{\mu_{f}+\mu_{g}}{2}-[F]_{\varepsilon}\right)_{v}+\frac{1}{2}(\mu_{f}-\mu_{g},\mu_{f}-\mu_{g})_{v}\geq\frac{1}{2}(\mu_{f}-\mu_{g},\mu_{f}-\mu_{g})_{v}. $$

Summing over $v\in M_{K}$ and using Proposition 3.16, we obtain

$$ \frac{1}{2}\langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle\leq\langle\mu_{f},[F]_{\varepsilon}\rangle+\langle\mu_{g},[F]_{\varepsilon}\rangle\leq\widehat{h}_{f}(x)+\widehat{h}_{g}(x)+O\left(d\frac{\log N}{N}(h(f)+h(g)+1)\right)\leq\widehat{h}_{f}(x)+\widehat{h}_{g}(x)+C_{d,f,g}\frac{\log N}{N}. $$

Now for any $\delta>0$ , choose $M$ sufficiently large such that $\frac{\log m}{m}\leq\frac{\delta}{C_{d,f,g}}$ for all $m\geq M$ . Then we have the implication

$$ \widehat{h}_{f}(x)+\widehat{h}_{g}(x)\leq\frac{1}{2}\langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle-\delta\implies N=[\mathbb{Q}(x):\mathbb{Q}]<M. $$

By Northcott’s theorem, there are only finitely many $x\in{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}$ satisfying both the hypothesis and our degree bound. Hence

$$ \liminf_{x\in{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}}\left(\widehat{h}_{f}(x)+\widehat{h}_{g}(x)\right)\geq\frac{1}{2}\langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle-\delta, $$

and we are done since $\delta>0$ is arbitrary. ∎

The proof of Proposition 6.2 also explains why it is not an equality in general. For (13) to be an equality, we must have $[F]\approx\frac{1}{2}(\mu_{f}+\mu_{g})$ at every place $v$ , but then $\sum_{v\in M_{K}}N_{v}([F],{F})_{v}\approx\sum_{v\in M_{K}}N_{v}\langle\mu_{f},\mu_{g}\rangle_{v}$ which is positive whenever $\mu_{f}\not=\mu_{g}$ , contradicting the product formula.

We now move onto the case of a generic pair. We start by controlling the archimedean place. Recall from Lemma 3.2 that $K_{f,\infty}\subseteq B(0,R_{f,\infty})$ , where $R_{f,\infty}=3\max(1,|a_{d-1}|_{\infty},|a_{d-2}|_{\infty}^{1/2},\ldots,|a_{0}|_{\infty}^{1/d})$ .

#### Lemma 6.3.

For any $\varepsilon$ -ordinary pair $(f,g)\in\mathcal{P}_{c}(X)\times\mathcal{P}(X)$ , we have $R_{f,\infty}\leq 3X^{\varepsilon}$ and $R_{g,\infty}\leq 3X^{2\varepsilon}$ .

#### Proof.

Since $f\in\mathcal{P}(X)$ , the numerator of $a_{j}$ has absolute value at most $X$ . Also, since $(f,g)$ is $\varepsilon$ -ordinary, we have $\operatorname{denom}(a_{j})\geq X^{1-2\varepsilon}$ . Hence $|a_{j}|_{\infty}\leq X^{2\varepsilon}$ , and now $a_{d-1}=0$ implies $R_{f,\infty}\leq 3X^{\varepsilon}$ . The argument for $g$ is analogous. ∎

The key step in the lower bound for $\liminf_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}(\widehat{h}_{f}+\widehat{h}_{g})$ is the following estimate on the sum of local heights, with an extra term $-\tfrac{1}{2}\log|x|_{v}$ which vanishes by the product formula when we sum over all places.

#### Lemma 6.4.

For any $\varepsilon$ -ordinary pair $(f,g)\in\mathcal{P}_{c}(X)\times\mathcal{P}(X)$ , and any $v\in M_{K}$ associated to $a_{j}$ , we have

$$ \inf_{x\in{\mathbb{A}^{1}_{\operatorname{Berk},v}}}\left(G_{f,v}(x)+G_{g,v}(x)-\tfrac{1}{2}\log|x|_{v}\right)=\begin{cases}\frac{1}{2(d-j)}\log|a_{j}|_{v}&j\leq\frac{d-1}{2},\\
\frac{d-j-1}{2j(d-j)}\log|a_{j}|_{v}&j\geq\frac{d-1}{2}.\end{cases} $$

The same statement holds with $a_{j}$ replaced by $b_{j}$ .

#### Proof.

Let $\psi_{v}(\zeta)=G_{f,v}(\zeta)+G_{g,v}(\zeta)-\frac{1}{2}\log|\zeta|_{v}$ . Since $\psi_{v}(\zeta)\to\infty$ as $|\zeta|_{v}\to\infty$ , the minimum value of $\psi_{v}$ occurs on the support of the positive part of $\triangle\psi_{v}$ , which is $J_{f,v}\cup\{\zeta(0,1)\}$ . Now $v$ is associated to $a_{j}$ , so $g$ has explicit good reduction at $v$ , and thus $G_{g,v}=\log^{+}|\cdot|_{v}$ . Hence we can compute the value of $\psi_{v}$ at each of the three strata of $J_{f,v}$ (Theorem 5.24) and at $\zeta(0,1)$ (Corollary 5.25), as follows:

$$ \begin{array}[]{*5c}|\zeta|_{v}&G_{f,v}(\zeta)&G_{g,v}(\zeta)&\log|\zeta|_{v}&\psi_{v}(\zeta)\\
\hline\cr r_{1}&0&\frac{1}{d-j}\log|a_{j}|_{v}&\frac{1}{d-j}\log|a_{j}|_{v}&\frac{1}{2(d-j)}\log|a_{j}|_{v}\\
1&\frac{1}{d}\log|a_{j}|_{v}&0&0&\frac{1}{d}\log|a_{j}|_{v}\\
r_{2}&0&0&\frac{1}{j}(\frac{1}{d-j}-1)\log|a_{j}|_{v}&\frac{1}{2j}(1-\frac{1}{d-j})\log|a_{j}|_{v}\\
r_{3}&0&0&-\frac{1}{j}\log|a_{j}|_{v}&\frac{1}{2j}\log|a_{j}|_{v}\end{array} $$

Since $\frac{2}{d}\geq\min(\frac{1}{j},\frac{1}{d-j})$ , and $\frac{1}{j}>\frac{1}{j}(1-\frac{1}{d-j})$ , we have

$$ \inf_{\mathbb{A}^{1}_{\operatorname{Berk},v}}\psi_{v}=\min\left(\tfrac{1}{2j}\left(1-\tfrac{1}{d-j}\right),\tfrac{1}{2(d-j)}\right)\log|a_{j}|_{v}, $$

which is equivalent to the claim. The argument for $b_{j}$ is analogous. ∎

#### Theorem 6.5.

For any $\varepsilon$ -ordinary pair $(f,g)\in\mathcal{P}_{c}(X)\times\mathcal{P}(X)$ , we have

$$ \inf_{x\in{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}\setminus\{0\}}\left(\widehat{h}_{f}(x)+\widehat{h}_{g}(x)\right)\geq 2\left(\log 2-O(d^{2}\varepsilon+\tfrac{\log d}{d})\right)\log X-O(1). $$

#### Proof.

Let $K$ be a number field with $x\in K\setminus\{0\}$ . For any $v\in M_{K}$ , write $\psi_{v}(x)=G_{f,v}(x)+G_{g,v}(x)-\frac{1}{2}\log|x|_{v}$ . Then by the product formula $\sum_{v\in M_{K}}n_{v}\log|x|_{v}=0$ , we have

$$ \widehat{h}_{f}(x)+\widehat{h}_{g}(x)=\frac{1}{[K:\mathbb{Q}]}\sum_{v\in M_{K}}\!n_{v}\psi_{v}(x), $$

We split the sum over good, bad, and archimedean places. For good places, by Lemma 6.4 we have

$$ \frac{1}{[K:\mathbb{Q}]}\sum_{v\in M_{K}\text{ good}}\!\!n_{v}\psi_{v}(x)\geq\frac{1}{[K:\mathbb{Q}]}\left(\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}v\text{ assoc.\ }a_{j}\\
0<j\leq\frac{d-1}{2}\end{subarray}}\!\!n_{v}\frac{1}{2(d-j)}\log|a_{j}|_{v}+\!\!\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}v\text{ assoc.\ }b_{j}\\
0<j\leq\frac{d-1}{2}\end{subarray}}\!\!n_{v}\frac{1}{2(d-j)}\log|b_{j}|_{v}\right. $$

$$ +\left.\!\!\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}v\text{ assoc.\ }a_{j}\\
\frac{d-1}{2}<j<d\end{subarray}}\!\!n_{v}\frac{d-j-1}{2j(d-j)}\log|a_{j}|_{v}+\!\!\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}v\text{ assoc.\ }b_{j}\\
\frac{d-1}{2}<j<d\end{subarray}}\!\!n_{v}\frac{d-j-1}{2j(d-j)}\log|b_{j}|_{v}\right). $$

By Lemma 5.17, this is

$$ \geq 2(1-O(d\varepsilon))\left(\sum_{0<j\leq\frac{d-1}{2}}\frac{1}{2(d-j)}+\sum_{\frac{d-1}{2}<j<d}\frac{d-j-1}{2j(d-j)}\right)\log X. $$

We recognize the first sum in (14) as a Riemann sum:

$$ \sum_{0<j\leq\frac{d-1}{2}}\frac{1}{2(d-j)}\geq\int_{0}^{1/2}\frac{1}{2(1-t)}dt-O\left(\frac{1}{d}\right)=\frac{\log 2}{2}-O\left(\frac{1}{d}\right). $$

The summand in the second sum of (14) splits into $\frac{1}{2j}-\frac{1}{2j(d-j)}$ . As before,

$$ \sum_{\frac{d-1}{2}<j<d}\frac{1}{2j}\geq\int_{1/2}^{1}\frac{1}{2t}dt-O\left(\frac{1}{d}\right)=\frac{\log 2}{2}-O\left(\frac{1}{d}\right), $$

while

$$ \sum_{\frac{d-1}{2}<j<d}\frac{1}{2j(d-j)}\leq\sum_{\frac{d-1}{2}<j<d}\frac{1}{j(d-j)}\leq O\left(\frac{\log d}{d}\right). $$

Substituting (15), (16), (17) back into (14), we have

$$ \frac{1}{[K:\mathbb{Q}]}\sum_{v\in M_{K}\text{ good}}\!\!n_{v}\psi_{v}(x)\geq 2(1-O(d\varepsilon))\left(\log 2-O(\tfrac{\log d}{d})\right)\log X $$

$$ \geq 2\left(\log 2-O(d\varepsilon+\tfrac{\log d}{d})\right)\log X. $$

For bad places, we have $K_{f,v}\subseteq\overline{D}_{\operatorname{an}}(0,R_{f,v})\subseteq\overline{D}_{\operatorname{an}}(0,\mathcal{M}_{f,v})$ by Proposition 3.9, and similarly for $g$ . Hence $G_{f,v}(x)=G_{g,v}(x)=\log^{+}|x|_{v}$ for all $x$ such that $|x|_{v}>\max(\mathcal{M}_{f,v},\mathcal{M}_{g,v})$ . Therefore

$$ \psi_{v}(x)\geq\begin{cases}\tfrac{3}{2}\log|x|_{v}&\text{if }|x|_{v}>\max(\mathcal{M}_{f,v},\mathcal{M}_{g,v})\\
-\frac{1}{2}\log\max(\mathcal{M}_{f,v},\mathcal{M}_{g,v})&\text{if }|x|_{v}\leq\max(\mathcal{M}_{f,v},\mathcal{M}_{g,v}).\end{cases} $$

Hence using Proposition 5.20,

$$ \frac{1}{[K:\mathbb{Q}]}\sum_{v\in M_{K}\text{ bad}}\!\!n_{v}\psi_{v}(x)\geq-\frac{1}{2[K:\mathbb{Q}]}\sum_{v\in M_{K}\text{ bad}}\!\!n_{v}\left(\log\mathcal{M}_{f,v}+\log\mathcal{M}_{g,v}\right)\geq-O(d^{2}\varepsilon)\log X. $$

For archimedean places $v\mid\infty$ we split into two cases. If $|x|_{v}\leq R_{f,\infty}+1$ then

$$ \psi_{v}(x)\geq-\tfrac{1}{2}\log|x|_{v}\geq-\tfrac{1}{2}\log(R_{f,\infty}+1). $$

If $|x|_{v}\geq R_{f,\infty}+1$ , then for all $w\in K_{f,v}$ we have $|w/x|_{v}\leq R_{f,\infty}/(R_{f,\infty}+1)$ , so

$$ G_{f,v}(x)-\log|x|_{v}\geq\int\log|\frac{x-w}{x}|_{v}d\mu_{f,v}(w)\geq-\log(R_{f,\infty}+1), $$

and thus

$$ \psi_{v}(x)\geq\frac{1}{2}(G_{f,v}(x)-\log|x|_{v})\geq-\frac{1}{2}\log(R_{f,\infty}+1). $$

In either case, by Lemma 6.3, we have

$$ \frac{1}{[K:\mathbb{Q}]}\sum_{v\mid\infty}n_{v}\psi_{v}(x)\geq-\frac{1}{2}\log(R_{f,\infty}+1)=-O(\varepsilon\log X+1). $$

Adding (18), (19) and (20) yields the desired bound. ∎

We now prove our upper bound of $\liminf\widehat{h}_{f}(x)+\widehat{h}_{g}(x)$ , which is improves Proposition 6.1 by a constant. As in the proof of Proposition 6.1, we need to construct infinitely many $x\in{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}$ such that $\widehat{h}_{f}(x)+\widehat{h}_{g}(x)$ is small. Our main tool will be Theorem 6.7, which is a special case of the adelic Fekete–Szegő theorem [Rum13, Thm. 0.4].

#### Definition 6.6.

A compact Berkovich adelic set $\mathbb{E}=(E_{v})_{v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}}$ is a collection of compact affinoids $E_{v}\subseteq{\mathbb{A}^{1}_{\operatorname{Berk},v}}$ for each place $v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}$ , with $E_{v}=\overline{D}_{\operatorname{an}}(0,1)$ for all but finitely many $v$ . The Robin constant $V(\mathbb{E})$ of $\mathbb{E}$ is $V(\mathbb{E}):=\sum_{v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}}V(E_{v})$ .

#### Theorem 6.7.

Let $\mathbb{E}=(E_{v})_{v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}}$ be a compact Berkovich adelic set. If $V(\mathbb{E})\geq 0$ , then there exists infinitely many $x\in\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ such that the $\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$ -orbit of $x$ lies inside $E_{v}$ at every place $v$ .

Our strategy is to construct, given any $\varepsilon$ -ordinary $(f,g)$ , a compact Berkovich adelic set $\mathbb{E}$ with $V(\mathbb{E})>0$ and $\sum_{v}n_{v}\sup_{x\in E_{v}}\left(G_{f}(x)+G_{g}(x)\right)$ small.

#### Theorem 6.8.

For any $\varepsilon$ -ordinary pair $(f,g)\in\mathcal{P}_{c}(X)\times\mathcal{P}(X)$ , we have

$$ \liminf_{x\in{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}}\left(\widehat{h}_{f}(x)+\widehat{h}_{g}(x)\right)\leq 2\left(\mathcal{C}+O(d\varepsilon+\tfrac{1}{d})\right)\log X+O(1), $$

where $\mathcal{C}=\log\left(\frac{9+\sqrt{17}}{8}\right)+\frac{\sqrt{17}-1}{8}=0.88532\ldots$

#### Proof.

Let $\alpha:=\frac{\sqrt{17}-1}{8}$ , and let $c>0$ be a small parameter to be chosen later. We consider the adelic set $\mathbb{E}=(E_{v})_{v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}}$ given by

$$ E_{v}\coloneqq\begin{cases}S_{f,v}^{\cup}&v\text{ assoc.\ }a_{j}\text{ with }0<\frac{j}{d}<\alpha+c,\\
S_{g,v}^{\cup}&v\text{ assoc.\ }b_{j}\text{ with }0<\frac{j}{d}<\alpha+c,\\
S_{f,v}^{\cap}&v\text{ assoc.\ }a_{j}\text{ with }2\alpha<\frac{j}{d}<1,\\
S_{g,v}^{\cap}&v\text{ assoc.\ }b_{j}\text{ with }2\alpha<\frac{j}{d}<1,\\
\overline{D}_{\operatorname{an}}(0,1)&\text{otherwise},\end{cases} $$

with $S_{f,v}^{\cup},S_{f,v}^{\cap}$ as defined in Proposition 5.27. Using Proposition 5.27 and Lemma 5.17, we bound $V(\mathbb{E})$ from below:

$$ V(\mathbb{E})=\sum_{v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}}\!V(E_{v})=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}v\text{ assoc.\ }a_{j}\\
0<\frac{j}{d}<\alpha+c\end{subarray}}\frac{1}{2(d-j)}\log|a_{j}|_{v}+\!\!\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}v\text{ assoc.\ }b_{j}\\
0<\frac{j}{d}<\alpha+c\end{subarray}}\frac{1}{2(d-j)}\log|b_{j}|_{v} $$

$$ -\!\!\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}v\text{ assoc.\ }a_{j}\\
2\alpha<\frac{j}{d}<1\end{subarray}}\frac{1}{j}\log|a_{j}|_{v}-\!\!\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}v\text{ assoc.\ }b_{j}\\
2\alpha<\frac{j}{d}<1\end{subarray}}\frac{1}{j}\log|b_{j}|_{v}\geq\left(2-O(d\varepsilon)\right)\log X\!\!\sum_{0<\frac{j}{d}<\alpha+c}\frac{1}{2(d-j)}-2\log X\!\!\sum_{2\alpha<\frac{j}{d}<1}\frac{1}{j}. $$

We recognize the sums above as Riemann sums:

$$ \sum_{0<\frac{j}{d}<\alpha+c}\frac{1}{2(d-j)}\geq\int_{0}^{\alpha+c}\frac{1}{2(1-t)}dt-O\left(\frac{1}{d}\right)=\frac{\log(1-\alpha-c)}{2}-O\left(\frac{1}{d}\right), $$

$$ \sum_{2\alpha<\frac{j}{d}<1}\frac{1}{j}\geq\int_{2\alpha}^{1}\frac{1}{t}dt-O\left(\frac{1}{d}\right)=\log(2\alpha)-O\left(\frac{1}{d}\right). $$

Hence

$$ V(\mathbb{E})\geq\left(-\left(1-O(d\varepsilon)\right)\log(1-\alpha-c)-2\log(2\alpha)-O(\tfrac{1}{d})\right)\log X\geq\left(\Theta(c)-O(d\varepsilon+\tfrac{1}{d})\right)\log X, $$

where we have used the identity $-\frac{1}{2}\log(1-\alpha)=\log(2\alpha)$ . Hence we may choose $c=O(d\varepsilon+\frac{1}{d})$ so that $V(\mathbb{E})\geq 0$ .

We want to apply the adelic Fekete–Szegő theorem to $\mathbb{E}$ , but the issue is that $S_{f,v}^{\cup},S_{f,v}^{\cap}$ are not Berkovich affinoids. To fix this, we construct a new adelic set $\widetilde{\mathbb{E}}=(\widetilde{E}_{v})_{v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}}$ by replacing the sets $S_{f,v}^{\cup},S_{f,v}^{\cap}$ in the definition of $\mathbb{E}$ by compact affinoids $\widetilde{S}_{f,v}^{\cup}\supseteq S_{f,v}^{\cup}$ and $\widetilde{S}_{f,v}^{\cap}\supseteq S_{f,v}^{\cap}$ such that

$$ \sup_{\widetilde{S}_{f,v}^{\cup}}(G_{f,v}+\log^{+}|\cdot|_{v})\leq\frac{1}{d-j}\log|a_{j}|_{v}+\eta,\qquad\sup_{\widetilde{S}_{f,v}^{\cap}}(G_{f,v}+\log^{+}|\cdot|_{v})\leq\eta, $$

where $\eta>0$ is a small parameter to be chosen later. (This is possible by Proposition 5.27, and the fact that $G_{f,v}+\log^{+}|\cdot|_{v}$ is continuous on ${\mathbb{A}^{1}_{\operatorname{Berk},v}}$ .) Similarly, we also replace $S_{g,v}^{\cup},S_{g,v}^{\cap}$ with closed neighborhoods $\widetilde{S}_{g,v}^{\cup},\widetilde{S}_{g,v}^{\cap}$ .

Now $\widetilde{\mathbb{E}}$ is a compact Berkovich adelic set and $V(\widetilde{\mathbb{E}})\geq V(\mathbb{E})\geq 0$ , so by Theorem 6.7 we can find infinitely many distinct $x_{n}\in{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}$ whose $\operatorname{Gal}({\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}/\mathbb{Q})$ -orbit $F_{n}$ lies entirely in $\widetilde{\mathbb{E}}$ .

Let $K_{n}$ be a number field containing $F_{n}$ . The local contribution to $\widehat{h}_{f}(x_{n})$ at $v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}$ is

$$ \frac{1}{[K_{n}:\mathbb{Q}]}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}v^{\prime}\in M_{K_{n}}\\
v^{\prime}\mid v\end{subarray}}\!\!n_{v^{\prime}}G_{f,v^{\prime}}(x_{n})=\frac{1}{|F_{n}|}\sum_{x\in F_{n}}G_{f,v}(x)\leq\sup_{\widetilde{E}_{v}}G_{f,v}, $$

and similarly for $g$ . Hence we are left to bound $\sup_{\widetilde{E}_{v}}(G_{f,v}+G_{g,v})$ from above at good, bad, and archimedean places $v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}$ .

For good places $v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}$ , if $v$ is associated to $a_{j}$ then $g$ has good reduction at $v$ , so $G_{f,v}+G_{g,v}=G_{f,v}+\log^{+}|\cdot|_{v}$ , and we are in the setting of Proposition 5.27 and (21). If $v$ is associated to $b_{j}$ , we use the analogous statements with $f,g$ swapped. Working through the possible cases in terms of $j$ , we have

$$ \sup_{\widetilde{E}_{v}}(G_{f,v}+G_{g,v})\leq\begin{cases}\frac{1}{d-j}\log|a_{j}|_{v}+\eta&v\text{ assoc.\ }a_{j}\text{ with }0<\frac{j}{d}<\alpha+c,\\
\frac{1}{d-j}\log|b_{j}|_{v}+\eta&v\text{ assoc.\ }b_{j}\text{ with }0<\frac{j}{d}<\alpha+c,\\
\frac{1}{d}\log|a_{j}|_{v}&v\text{ assoc.\ }a_{j}\text{ with }\alpha+c<\frac{j}{d}<2\alpha,\\
\frac{1}{d}\log|b_{j}|_{v}&v\text{ assoc.\ }b_{j}\text{ with }\alpha+c<\frac{j}{d}<2\alpha,\\
\eta&v\text{ assoc.\ }a_{j}\text{ or }b_{j}\text{ with }2\alpha<\frac{j}{d}<1.\end{cases} $$

or bad places $v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}$ , we have by Lemma 5.6 and Lemma 5.5,

$$ \sup_{\overline{D}_{\operatorname{an}}(0,1)}(G_{f,v}+G_{g,v})\leq G_{f,v}(\zeta(0,1))+G_{g,v}(\zeta(0,1))=\frac{1}{d}(\log\mathcal{M}_{f,v}+\log\mathcal{M}_{g,v}). $$

Finally, for the archimedean place, we have $\widetilde{E}_{\infty}=\partial B(0,1)$ , so for any $z\in\widetilde{E}_{\infty}$ and $w\in K_{f,\infty}$ we have $|z-w|\leq R_{f,\infty}+1$ , with $R_{f,\infty}$ as in Lemma 3.2. Thus

$$ G_{f,\infty}(z)=\int\log|z-w|_{\infty}d\mu_{f,\infty}(w)\leq\log(R_{f,\infty}+1), $$

and similarly for $g$ . Hence by Lemma 6.3 we have

$$ \sup_{\partial B(0,1)}(G_{f,\infty}+G_{g,\infty})\leq\log(R_{f,\infty}+1)+\log(R_{g,\infty}+1)\leq O(\varepsilon\log X+1). $$

Now we choose $\eta\leq\#\{\text{good places }v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}\}^{-1}$ , so

$$ \widehat{h}_{f}(x_{n})+\widehat{h}_{g}(x_{n})\leq\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}v\text{ assoc.\ }a_{j}\\
0<\frac{j}{d}<\alpha+c\end{subarray}}\frac{1}{d-j}\log|a_{j}|_{v}+\!\!\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}v\text{ assoc.\ }b_{j}\\
0<\frac{j}{d}<\alpha+c\end{subarray}}\frac{1}{d-j}\log|b_{j}|_{v} $$

$$ +\!\!\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}v\text{ assoc.\ }a_{j}\\
\alpha+c<\frac{j}{d}<2\alpha\end{subarray}}\frac{1}{d}\log|a_{j}|_{v}+\!\!\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}v\text{ assoc.\ }b_{j}\\
\alpha+c<\frac{j}{d}<2\alpha\end{subarray}}\frac{1}{d}\log|b_{j}|_{v}+\frac{1}{d}\sum_{v\text{ bad}}(\log\mathcal{M}_{f,v}+\log\mathcal{M}_{g,v})+O(\varepsilon\log X+1). $$

By Proposition 5.20, this is

$$ \leq\left(2\!\!\sum_{0<\frac{j}{d}<\alpha+c}\!\!\frac{1}{d-j}+2\!\!\sum_{\alpha+c<\frac{j}{d}<2\alpha}\!\!\frac{1}{d}+O(d\varepsilon)\right)\log X+O(1). $$

The first sum is a Riemann sum as before, and the second sum is easy to bound:

$$ \widehat{h}_{f}(x_{n})+\widehat{h}_{g}(x_{n})\leq\left(-2\log(1-\alpha-c)+2(\alpha-c)+O(d\varepsilon+\tfrac{1}{d})\right)\log X+O(1) $$

$$ =2\left(\mathcal{C}+O\left(c+d\varepsilon+\tfrac{1}{d}\right)\right)\log X+O(1), $$

where $\mathcal{C}=-\log(1-\alpha)+\alpha$ , and we are done since $c=O(d\varepsilon+\frac{1}{d})$ . ∎

Putting together Theorems 6.5 and 6.8, we obtain Theorem 1.6. Recall that we define $\cal{P}$ and $\cal{P}_{c}$ to be the space of monic polynomials and monic centered polynomials with rational coefficients respectively.

#### Proof.

Let $\delta>0$ be given. Then for all large enough $d$ depending on $\delta$ , we can choose $\epsilon$ small enough depending on $d$ such that the terms $O(d\epsilon+\frac{1}{d}),O(d^{2}\epsilon+\frac{\log d}{d})$ and $O(d\epsilon+\frac{1}{d})$ occurring in Proposition 5.18, Theorem 6.5 and Theorem 6.8 respectively are bounded above by $\frac{\delta}{3}$ .

Let $X$ be sufficiently large such that for the terms $O(1)$ ’s occuring in Theorem 6.5 and Theorem 6.8, we have $\frac{\delta}{3}\log X\geq O(1)$ . Then by Theorem 6.5 and Theorem 6.8, we know that for any $\varepsilon$ -ordinary pair $(f,g)\in\cal{S}(X)$ we have

$$ 2\left(\ln 2-\frac{2}{3}\delta\right)\log X\leq\liminf_{x\in\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}\left(\widehat{h}_{f}(x)+\widehat{h}_{g}(x)\right)\leq 2\left(\cal{C}+\frac{2}{3}\delta\right)\log X. $$

Now Proposition 5.18 implies that for an $\varepsilon$ -ordinary pair of $\cal{S}(X)$ , we have

$$ h(f)+h(g)\geq d\left(2-\frac{1}{3}\delta\right)\log X. $$

We also have the trivial upper bound

$$ h(f)+h(g)\leq 2d\log X $$

since each coefficient of $f$ and $g$ have height bounded by $\log X$ and we have at most $2d$ different coefficients. We now assume $\delta$ is small enough so that

$$ \left(2-\frac{1}{3}\delta\right)(\cal{C}+\delta)\geq 2\left(\cal{C}+\frac{2}{3}\delta\right). $$

This is possible since $\cal{C}<1$ . Then substituting in our bounds of $h(f)+h(g)$ against $\log X$ , we obtain

$$ (\ln 2-\delta)(h(f)+h(g))\leq d\liminf_{x\in\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}\left(\widehat{h}_{f}(x)+\widehat{h}_{g}(x)\right)\leq(\cal{C}+\delta)(h(f)+h(g)) $$

for all $\varepsilon$ -ordinary pairs $(f,g)\in\cal{S}(X)$ , if $X$ is sufficiently large. By Proposition 5.15, the proportion of $\varepsilon$ -ordinary pairs in $\cal{S}(X)$ is at least $1-O_{\epsilon}(d^{2}X^{-\epsilon})$ . Clearly we can take $\epsilon=\frac{c}{d^{2}}$ for some constant $c>0$ that depends on $\delta$ and so the proportion of $\varepsilon$ -ordinary pairs will be $1-O_{d}(d^{2}X^{-c/d^{2}})$ . Finally, we set $\cal{T}$ to be the all pairs $(f,g)$ which are $\varepsilon$ -ordinary for some $X$ which is sufficiently large for our previous bounds to hold. Then

$$ \frac{|\cal{T}\cap\cal{S}(X)|}{|\cal{S}(X)|}\geq 1-\frac{A}{X^{a}} $$

for some constants $a=a(d)>0,A=A(d)>0$ that depend on the degree $d$ , and

$$ (\ln 2-\delta)(h(f)+h(g))\leq d\liminf_{x\in\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}\left(\widehat{h}_{f}(x)+\widehat{h}_{g}(x)\right)\leq(\cal{C}+\delta)(h(f)+h(g)) $$

for all $(f,g)\in\cal{T}$ as desired.
